title: Fleet order triage and lead-time decision log
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures the triage decisions we make for incoming GPU orders, the SKU mix choices by region, and the lead-time buckets we are using to adjust safety buffers. It is intentionally pragmatic — a compact ledger to justify order splits, cancellations, and expedited requests when utilization shifts or arrivals slip.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Current committed fleet: 12.4k A100-equivalent cards across US-W, US-E, EU-W, APAC.
- Near-term deficit signal: projected 9% shortage on peak inference lanes in US-W for January–March due to higher-than-modeled usage on hosted API (streaming).
- Procurement actions recommended: expedite 480 cards (mixed A100-80GB / A10G) into US-W (arrival target: 2026-04), stagger remaining tranche into EU-W and APAC to preserve global hedges.
- Risk posture: maintain 11% cold spare for Dedicated contractual windows; reduce to 8% only if we secure 7-day accelerated shipping windows.

Assumptions and definitions:
- A100-equivalent: normalizes different SKUs by inference throughput for 2k token sequences.
- Safety buffer: % of fleet reserved to absorb demand shock and lead-time slippage (measured per-region).
- Arrival slippage buckets: on-time (0–7 days), short slip (8–21 days), long slip (22+ days).
- Order lanes: Standard (90–120 day lead), Accelerated (30–45 day lead), Expedited (<14 day lead).

SKU-mix rationale (high level):
- A100-80GB: primary for high-throughput hosted streaming workloads; expensive but best latency/throughput.
- A10G: good cost/perf for batch embeddings and lower-concurrency dedicated customers.
- H100 (spot hedges): test small fraction for quantized LLMs where half-precision performance matters.

SKU allocation table (text rows representing sheet columns):
- Region | Target % of new orders | Primary SKU | Secondary SKU | Safety buffer target
- US-West | 42% | A100-80GB | A10G | 11%
- US-East | 18% | A100-80GB | A10G | 9%
- EU-West | 22% | A10G | H100 | 12%
- APAC | 18% | A10G | A100-80GB | 14%

Order pipeline snapshot (most recent tranches):
- PO# 2026-Q1-07 | 1,200 cards | SKU mix: 70% A100-80GB / 30% A10G | Regions: US-W(60%), EU-W(25%), APAC(15%) | ETD factory: 2026-02-18 | ETA earliest: 2026-05-03 | Current status: in vendor hold (pricing reconciliation).
- PO# 2026-Q1-12 | 600 cards | SKU mix: 100% A10G | Regions: EU-W(60%), APAC(40%) | ETD factory: 2026-01-05 | ETA earliest: 2026-04-22 | Current status: shipping booked (partial manifest).
- PO# 2026-accelerate-01 | 480 cards | SKU mix: 50% A100-80GB / 50% A10G | Regions: US-W 100% | ETD factory: 2026-03-01 | ETA earliest: 2026-04-02 | Current status: expedite request with freight (pending budget approval).

Lead time estimates (vendor-averaged, updated 2026-02):
- Standard channel (baseline OEM): 90–120 days (median 104).
- OEM prioritized channel: 45–60 days (median 52) with confirmed MOQ and landing slots.
- Freight-expedite (air/charter): 7–18 days (median 12) but 3× cost multiplier.
- Customs + regional staging: add 7–14 days to ETA depending on port congestion at destination.

Arrival slippage impact model (cheat-sheet):
- If >15% of scheduled arrivals slip to long-slip, increase regional safety buffer target by 3–5ppt and temporarily shift new orders into Accelerated lane.
- If expedited orders are used >2x per quarter, escalate to Finance for a temporary P&L approval to reallocate freight budget.

Decision triage matrix (how to choose lane / split):
- Trigger: host-tier 95th percentile latency upward shift + utilization > 72% sustained for 7 days -> escalate to "accelerate" lane for US regions only.
- Trigger: Dedicated reserved capacity approaching SLA threshold with <6 week replenishment window -> re-prioritize all A10G tranches to Dedicated heavy regions.
- Finance gating: any expedite that costs >$150k incremental must be signed off by Head of Revenue Ops.

Recent decisions and justifications (log):
- 2026-02-10: moved PO#2026-Q1-07 into vendor hold while renegotiating lead time credits due to 9-day factory delay. Rationale: keep total cost within planned unit economics and avoid stacking expedited fees. (Owner: Marcus Chen)
- 2026-02-17: approved partial expedite for 480-card tranche to US-W conditioned on approval of $132k freight spend and confirmation of 14-day customs lane. Rationale: avoid spike-related SLA breaches for hosted streaming. (Owner: Aisha Malik)

Regional utilization & action thresholds (quick reference):
- US-West: current fleet util 74% (90-day rolling peak 81%). Action: accelerate 480 cards into US-W; re-evaluate after 6 weeks of arrival to see if remaining 2026-Q2 commits are needed.
- US-East: current util 62% (peak 69%). Action: delay non-urgent A100 purchases by 30 days and reallocate 20% of APAC A10G tranche if APAC slips.
- EU-West: current util 58% (peak 64%). Action: confirm customs staging slots for April arrivals; consider swapping 10% of A10G to H100 trial for quantized model testbeds.
- APAC: current util 68% (peak 75% in SE-Asia). Action: hold 15% of incoming A10G tranche in vendor staging until clearer demand signal from Jakarta deployment.

Open questions / risks to resolve:
- Vendor invoice timing variability: some suppliers invoice on ETD rather than ETA; we need clear P&L month mapping and Finance sign-off to avoid working-capital surprises.
- H100 availability: small hedges useful but supply volatility and pricing spike risk; recommend option-based MOQs not firm purchases.
- Port congestion sensitivity: if Rotterdam/LA congestion index > 0.7 during March–May window, we should pre-book accelerated rail/air slots.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Aisha: finalize expedited freight PO and confirm $132k budget line with Finance by 2026-03-05.
- Marcus: negotiate lead-time credit clause with OEM for PO#2026-Q1-07 by 2026-03-01.
- Priya: validate customs staging times with our EU logistics partner and add contingency lane options by 2026-02-24 (done, see linked manifest).
- Tomasz: prepare rotation plan for decomm/reuse of old A100-40GB cards for internal training clusters by 2026-03-15.

Notes to procurement / vendor leads (bullet points):
- Request written confirmation of ETD and factory hold windows; include slippage credit terms in all new POs.
- Ask vendors for split manifests (by SKU per pallet) to speed customs pre-clearance.
- For any expedite request, provide three landing scenarios (fast / median / slow) and associated incremental cost so Finance can pre-approve conditional lanes.

Slack refs and attachments: #infra-procurement (thread: 2026-02-16 expedite ask), vendor manifests (s3://redwood-internal/manifests/2026-q1/), procurement playbook (linked above).

Appendix — quick numerical snapshot (rounded):
- Committed (ordered, not delivered): 3,280 cards total across active POs.
- Available cold spare across fleet: 1,360 cards (~11%).
- Projected burn (90d): 1,920 cards (based on current run rate + planned rollouts).
- Recommended expedite to avoid SLOs: 480 cards to US-W (as above).

Notes to reviewer: this is a working ledger and not final procurement instruction. Please flag any financial gating items or alternate vendor lanes you want us to consider; we will record decisions here and update the triage log weekly.
